data.body:
THE TWO MISSING TESTS ARE WRITTEN — Gerrit change 1183
(https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1183), commit cabaca5201 on its own branch off
origin/main so it lands independently of the J11 stack.

THE CLOSE GATE WAS RIGHT AND MY EARLIER READ WAS WRONG. I first attempted to close this ticket
on the strength of the merged fix alone. The verifier returned two unmet criteria, and on
inspection both were GENUINE GAPS rather than undocumented evidence: commit 7e3c50242d changed
`sys.modules.setdefault(name, mod)` to `sys.modules[name] = mod` and made the diffing suites'
`_load_module` cache-first, and it shipped with NO test of either half. Recording that here
because "the change merged with two green votes" is not the same claim as "the behaviour is
pinned", and this ticket is the second time this session that distinction mattered.

WHAT IS NOW PINNED — two invariants that pull in OPPOSITE directions, so each has its own cell
(`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/diffing/test_load_module_identity.py`):
  1. SAME name + SAME path returns the SAME object, and the same CLASS object. Asserting on the
     class too is the part that matters: two modules holding equal-but-distinct `Probe` classes
     is precisely the state that made `isinstance` answer False for one source file.
  2. SAME name + a DIFFERENT path must NOT return the cached module. This is the counterweight:
     "fixing" 9f0b by caching on the name alone would silently serve the wrong file's code, so
     the naive repair has to stay red too.

BOTH MUTATION-CHECKED — AND THE FIRST ATTEMPT WAS NOT GOOD ENOUGH, which is the most useful
thing on this ticket. Restoring the original `sys.modules.setdefault` left BOTH tests GREEN.
The reason is structural: cache-first short-circuits and returns before ever reaching the
registration line, so the defect is UNREACHABLE when the name is free. The real 9f0b needed the
name ALREADY HELD by a different-path module — only then does `setdefault` keep the OLD object
while `exec_module` runs and returns the NEW one, leaving the caller holding a module that is
not the one registered under its own name, which is how a self-referential import resolves to
the other object and yields two class objects. The assertion was moved into the different-path
cell, where that state actually exists.
FINAL VERDICTS: `setdefault` restored -> the different-path cell FAILS naming the sys.modules
mismatch. `__file__` guard dropped -> it FAILS naming the wrong returned file. Unmutated ->
both PASS. `test_differ.py` restored byte-clean after each mutation (`git diff --quiet`).

TWO DELIBERATE CHOICES. The helper is loaded from `test_differ.py` BY PATH rather than
re-implemented, so the test tracks the shipped code — a restated copy would keep passing while
the original rotted (the same reasoning `test_user_guide_commands.py` uses for parsing the
guide at runtime). And a fixture restores every `sys.modules` key the test adds: a test whose
subject is module-cache leakage must not itself leak.

GATES: `make lint` and `make typecheck` both pass. Awaiting LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1.
